title: The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture
coverage:
This was a partial audit. Of about 6700 lines of LaTeX, I fully read and checked these parts.
- Introduction and statements.
- All of preliminaries.tex: the large-width lemma, block extraction, the deficit law, the one-coordinate concentration lemma, the tensor kernel, and the determinant-cycle residue averages. I also checked the periodicity claim with an explicit Bezout construction.
- centres.tex up to adjusted hosts, including the density lemma. I verified the centre-kernel identity for Theta_ij algebraically and checked the exponent bookkeeping in the kernel summation (H0(alpha-u) > u-1/2, s = 1/2-eps > 1-u, c = 2u-1). I also checked the raw-row second-moment case, where the pair count equals m_L m_M + Theta delta delta.
- arithmetic.tex up to the lcm bound:
  - Selberg sieve lemma: roundoff Z^8, Markov truncation, and the two-row factor R_p^2.
  - Rotation alternative: all three denominator ranges, and the constants C2 >= 200.
  - The stripping and pivot structure of the lcm bound.
- tables.tex:
  - The mask-transition identities (pi_I(a) = R_p pi_I'(a) and pi_I(pa) = R_p^[nu>=2]/p pi_I'(a)) and the first-currency identity.
  - One-prime mass preservation, including the residual-scaled orbit means.
  - The clipping inequality x0 - N0 <= (x0^2 - sum x_D^2)/N0.
  - The variance budget (J_p as an orbit variance) and the broad-energy bound: the self-cost expansion, capacity bounds (4c c and p^-2), and the unequal-width Cauchy-Schwarz with a dyadic kernel.
  - The equidistribution lemma and the final finite-block contradiction. Its numbers check: .4mu V - eta_s V - mu M_-/20 >= .3 mu M_-, and C2 |U delta E|^{1/2} <= .25 mu M_-.
- The whole of consequences.tex: the mass transference corollary, including the case r_q not tending to 0 and the endpoint conventions.

I did not verify the following. They hold the hardest arithmetic and combinatorics, so the absence of a gap there is not established.
- direct.tex (1169 lines), sparse.tex, partitions.tex and joins.tex. I only skimmed their statement list.
- The small-scale extraction proposition in arithmetic.tex.
- prescriptions.tex.
- The virtual-marginals proposition in tables.tex.
main_claim: Fix a shift gamma in R and a finite-valued psi: N -> [0,inf). If sum_q phi(q)psi(q)/q diverges, then for almost every x, ||qx - gamma|| < psi(q) holds for infinitely many q. Numerators are unrestricted. A Hausdorff-measure version follows by mass transference.
